title: Volcanic Pyroclastic Flow Terrain Simulation
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a volcanic pyroclastic flow terrain simulation using Three.js and GLTFLoader. The simulation models a volcanic eruption with pyroclastic flows descending a procedural terrain, with a robot survivor navigating the hazard zone.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 80, 120) looking at origin.
- Add a directional light (warm orange, intensity 1.2) from above-left simulating volcanic glow, plus dim ambient light (0.3 intensity, reddish tint).
- Generate a procedural terrain using a PlaneGeometry(200, 200, 128, 128) with vertex displacement to form a volcanic cone centered at (0, 0, 0). The cone peak should reach y=60. Apply a gradient material: dark rock at base, reddish-brown mid, glowing orange near summit.
- Load 'robot.glb' using GLTFLoader. Place the robot at position (40, 0, 40) on the terrain surface. Scale it to fit the scene (scale ~3). The robot represents a survivor that the user controls to escape pyroclastic flows.
- OrbitControls for camera, but disable during robot movement.

## Pyroclastic Flow System
- Maintain an array of pyroclastic flow particles. Each flow is a cluster of 50-100 small sphere meshes (radius 0.3-0.8) with emissive orange/grey materials and slight transparency.
- Flows originate from the volcano summit and descend radially outward following terrain slope (gravity-driven). Use simplified physics: each particle has position, velocity, temperature, and mass.
- Temperature starts at 800°C at summit, cools at rate of 2°C per second. Particles below 200°C become inert (grey, no emissive).
- Total system energy (kinetic + potential) must be tracked. Energy is conserved within 5% tolerance (friction dissipation accounted as heat).
- Flow speed depends on terrain slope: steeper = faster. Max velocity capped at 25 units/sec.
- Particles that reach terrain boundary (±100 units) are removed from simulation.

## Robot Control & Interaction
- WASD keys move the robot across terrain surface. W=forward(-Z), S=back(+Z), A=left(-X), D=right(+X). Movement speed: 8 units/sec.
- Robot Y position always snaps to terrain height at its XZ position.
- Robot has a 'health' value starting at 100. If any pyroclastic particle is within distance 5 of robot and temperature > 300°C, health decreases by 0.5 per frame.
- Space bar activates a 'shield' mode for 3 seconds (cooldown 10 seconds). Shield halves damage taken. Shield shown as a translucent blue sphere around robot.
- 'R' key resets robot to starting position (40, 0, 40) and health to 100 (undo/reset).
- 'U' key undoes the last robot movement (stores last 20 positions in a history stack).

## Eruption Control
- A DOM button '#erupt-btn' triggers a new eruption wave (spawns 200 particles at summit).
- A DOM slider '#intensity-slider' (range 1-10, default 5) controls eruption intensity: multiplies initial particle velocity and count.
- A DOM button '#pause-btn' toggles simulation pause (particles freeze, robot still movable).
- A DOM button '#reset-all-btn' resets entire simulation: clears all particles, resets robot, resets counters.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left HUD overlay showing: Robot Health (with color bar green>yellow>red), Shield Status (ready/active/cooldown with timer), Active Particles count, System Temperature (average of all active particles), Total Energy value.
- '#sim-time' span showing elapsed simulation seconds (paused time excluded).
- '#particle-count' span with current active particle count.
- '#robot-health' span with current health value (1 decimal).
- '#avg-temp' span with average particle temperature.
- '#energy-display' span with total system energy.
- '#shield-status' span showing 'ready', 'active', or 'cooldown'.

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose the following on window.__3D_STATE__:
- simulationRunning: boolean
- paused: boolean
- simTime: number (seconds elapsed)
- robotPosition: {x, y, z}
- robotHealth: number
- shieldActive: boolean
- shieldCooldown: boolean
- shieldTimer: number (seconds remaining)
- particles: array of {x, y, z, temp, vx, vy, vz, active}
- activeParticleCount: number
- totalEnergy: number (kinetic + potential)
- initialEnergy: number (energy at eruption start for conservation check)
- avgTemperature: number
- eruptionCount: number (how many eruptions triggered)
- intensity: number (current slider value)
- robotHistory: array of {x, y, z} (last 20 positions)
- terrainHeightAt: function(x, z) returning terrain y at that point
- robotModelLoaded: boolean
- volcanoApexY: number
- maxVelocity: number (observed max particle velocity)

All numerical values must be NaN-free. Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Pyroclastic particles follow gravity along terrain slope. Total energy (KE + PE) conserved within 5% after accounting for friction-as-heat dissipation. Temperature decays linearly at 2°C/s from initial 800°C. Particles with temp < 200°C become inert. Max particle velocity capped at 25 units/sec. Robot health decreases by 0.5/frame when within distance 5 of hot (>300°C) particles, halved when shield active.
